questions.q: Which of the following is an oilseed crop?
questions.explanation: Groundnut seeds are crushed to obtain oil, so it is an oilseed crop.

questions.q: A sickle is a farm tool used for:
questions.explanation: A sickle has a curved blade and is used to cut mature crops by hand.

questions.q: The sprinkler system of irrigation is most useful for:
options: Uneven land where water is scarce
questions.explanation: A sprinkler gives water like rain, so it suits uneven land and saves water.

questions.q: Fertilisers are added to the soil mainly to:
options: Replace the nutrients that earlier crops have taken
Increase the number of earthworms only
questions.explanation: Crops take nutrients from the soil, and fertilisers and manure put them back.

questions.q: What is threshing, and how is it done on large farms?
questions.answer: Threshing is the separation of grain seeds from the dry stalks and husk of the harvested crop. On large farms it is done with a machine called a combine harvester, which also harvests the crop.
keyPoints: Separating grain from stalks and husk
questions.explanation: On small farms it can be done by beating the crop by hand.

questions.q: A field has become less fertile after chemical fertilisers have been used alone for many years. What is the best remedy?
options: Add more of the same fertiliser
Add manure and rotate the crops
questions.explanation: Manure adds humus, and crop rotation restores nutrients.

questions.q: Weeds should be removed from a crop field early because weeds:
options: Compete with the crop for nutrients, water and light, and may harbour pests
questions.explanation: Weeds take away resources and reduce the yield of the crop.

questions.q: Why do seeds need water in order to germinate?
questions.answer: Seeds take in water, which softens the seed coat and wakes up the embryo inside. The water also helps the stored food to be used by the growing seedling.
keyPoints: Stored food is used by the seedling
questions.explanation: Without water a seed remains dormant.

questions.q: Which of the following is a protozoan?
questions.explanation: Amoeba is a single-celled protozoan.

questions.q: Medicines that kill or stop the growth of bacteria are called:
questions.explanation: Antibiotics act against bacteria.

questions.q: Yeast is used in the commercial production of:
questions.explanation: Yeast ferments sugar into alcohol, which is used to make wine and beer.

questions.q: Dengue is spread by the:
questions.explanation: The Aedes mosquito carries the dengue virus.

questions.q: Name three methods of preserving food at home and say how each works.
questions.answer: Heating or cooking and refrigeration keep microbes from growing. Salting and adding sugar remove water, and adding oil or vinegar in pickles keeps air and microbes away.
questions.explanation: Preservation prevents spoilage by microorganisms.

questions.q: Sodium benzoate is added to jams and squashes in small amounts to:
questions.explanation: Chemical preservatives slow or stop the growth of microbes in food.

questions.q: Why are children given vaccines at an early age?
options: To prepare their body to fight diseases before they get infected
To cure a disease they already have
questions.explanation: Vaccines let the body make antibodies in advance.

questions.q: Why is it important to wash hands with soap before eating?
questions.answer: Our hands pick up microbes from the surroundings. Washing with soap removes them, so they do not enter the body with the food and cause diseases such as diarrhoea.
questions.explanation: Hygiene prevents the spread of germs.

questions.q: Fibres that are made from chemical substances in factories are called:
questions.explanation: Synthetic fibres are man-made, from chemicals.

questions.q: Which plastic is used to coat non-stick cookware?
questions.explanation: Teflon is slippery and heat resistant, so it is used as a non-stick coating.

questions.q: Which statement about polyester fabric is correct?
options: It absorbs a lot of water
It is made from a plant
It is heavy and always crumples
It is wrinkle-resistant and easy to wash
questions.explanation: Polyester crumples very little and dries fast, so it is popular for clothes.

questions.q: What is PET and what is it used for?
questions.answer: PET (polyethylene terephthalate) is a plastic that is light, strong and clear. It is used to make bottles and containers for drinks and food.
questions.explanation: PET is a widely used thermoplastic.

questions.q: Shirts are often made from a blend of cotton and polyester because the blend:
options: Combines the comfort of cotton with the wrinkle resistance of polyester
questions.explanation: Blended fabrics combine useful properties of both fibres.

questions.q: Which of the following habits helps to reduce plastic pollution?
options: Using a new plastic bag every time
questions.explanation: Reusing bags reduces the amount of plastic that is thrown away.

questions.q: How are synthetic fibres different from natural fibres in their source and properties?
questions.answer: Natural fibres such as cotton and wool come from plants and animals, whereas synthetic fibres such as nylon are made from chemicals in factories. Synthetic fibres are usually stronger, dry quickly and last longer, but they melt and catch fire easily.
keyPoints: Synthetic are strong, durable and quick drying but melt easily
questions.explanation: Both kinds have advantages and disadvantages.

questions.q: Which of the following metals is commonly used to make jewellery?
questions.explanation: Gold is a shiny, soft and unreactive metal used in jewellery.

questions.q: Which of the following is a metal?
questions.explanation: Aluminium is a metal. Oxygen, carbon and sulphur are non-metals.

questions.q: When carbon burns in air, the gas produced is:
questions.explanation: Carbon combines with oxygen to form carbon dioxide.

questions.q: Write two differences between metals and non-metals.
questions.answer: Metals are generally lustrous, malleable, ductile and good conductors of heat and electricity. Non-metals are generally dull, brittle if solid, and poor conductors of heat and electricity.
keyPoints: Metals are lustrous, malleable and ductile
Non-metals are dull, brittle and poor conductors
questions.explanation: There are a few exceptions, such as graphite and mercury.

questions.q: A student tries to bend a copper wire and a piece of coal. The wire bends but the coal breaks. This shows that:
options: Metals are ductile and malleable, whereas coal is brittle
questions.explanation: Metals can be bent or drawn without breaking, but solid non-metals break easily.

questions.q: A silver spoon left in the air for a long time becomes dark because:
options: It reacts with substances such as sulphur compounds in the air
The spoon gets heated by sunlight
questions.explanation: Silver forms a dark layer of tarnish by reacting with compounds in the air.

questions.q: Why are the handles of cooking pans made of plastic or wood instead of metal?
questions.answer: Metals are good conductors of heat, so a metal handle would become too hot to hold. Plastic and wood are poor conductors, so the handle remains cool enough to hold.
keyPoints: Plastic and wood are poor conductors
questions.explanation: Insulators keep the handle safe to touch.

questions.q: Petrol, diesel and kerosene are obtained from:
questions.explanation: Crude petroleum is refined to get petrol, diesel and kerosene.

questions.q: Coal is a:
questions.explanation: Coal is a black, hard, solid fuel.

questions.q: Which coal product is used for making naphthalene balls, dyes and paints?
questions.explanation: Many useful chemicals are made from coal tar.

questions.q: State two uses of coal.
questions.answer: Coal is used as a fuel in homes, in industries and in power plants to generate electricity. Its product, coke, is used in making steel.
questions.explanation: Coal is an important source of energy.

questions.q: Compared with petrol, vehicles that run on CNG:
questions.explanation: CNG burns more completely and is a cleaner fuel.

questions.q: In an oil-bearing rock, natural gas is found above the petroleum. This is because natural gas is:
questions.explanation: Natural gas is lighter than oil, so it collects above it.

questions.q: Why are coal and petroleum called fossil fuels?
questions.answer: They were formed from the remains of dead plants and animals, which were buried under the earth for millions of years. Heat and pressure turned them into fuels, as fossils form from old remains.
keyPoints: Formed from remains of dead organisms
questions.explanation: Fossil fuels are non-renewable.

questions.q: The lowest temperature at which a substance catches fire is called its:
questions.explanation: Each substance has its own ignition temperature.

questions.q: Which of the following catches fire very easily?
questions.explanation: Petrol has a very low ignition temperature and burns easily, so it is inflammable.

questions.q: Water is a suitable extinguisher for burning wood and paper because it:
options: Cools the material below its ignition temperature
questions.explanation: Water absorbs heat and brings the temperature below ignition temperature.

questions.q: Distinguish between combustible and non-combustible substances with two examples of each.
questions.answer: Combustible substances burn in air, such as wood and paper. Non-combustible substances do not burn, such as glass and stone.
questions.explanation: Combustibility depends on the substance.

questions.q: Carbon monoxide, produced in incomplete combustion, is dangerous because it:
options: Is a poisonous gas that has no colour or smell
questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide cannot be seen or smelt, and it is poisonous when breathed.

questions.q: Why can sand be used to put out a small fire?
options: It cuts off the supply of air and covers the burning material
questions.explanation: Sand covers the fire and keeps oxygen from reaching it.

questions.q: What is calorific value? Why is it important when we choose a fuel?
questions.answer: Calorific value is the amount of heat produced by the complete burning of 1 kg of a fuel, measured in kJ/kg. A fuel with a higher calorific value gives more heat for the same mass, so it is more efficient.
keyPoints: Heat from complete burning of 1 kg
Higher value means a better fuel
questions.explanation: Fuels are compared by calorific value.

questions.q: The plants and animals of a region are together called its:
questions.explanation: Flora refers to plants and fauna refers to animals.

questions.q: Cutting down trees to get land for farming or buildings is called:
questions.explanation: Deforestation is the clearing of forests.

questions.q: Animals that move from one region to another according to the season are called:
questions.explanation: Migratory animals travel regularly for food, climate or breeding.

questions.q: What is the Red Data Book and why is it important?
questions.answer: The Red Data Book is a record of species of plants and animals that are endangered or threatened with extinction. It helps in planning how to protect them.
questions.explanation: It is kept by conservation organisations.

questions.q: Which activity damages life in rivers and ponds the most?
options: Dumping industrial waste into the water
questions.explanation: Waste poisons the water and kills fish and plants.

questions.q: Why should we avoid buying articles made from animal skin or ivory?
options: Demand for them leads to poaching, which endangers species
questions.explanation: Buying them encourages hunting of wild animals.

questions.q: How can saving paper help to save forests?
questions.answer: Paper is made from wood pulp, which comes from trees. If we use less paper and reuse or recycle it, fewer trees are cut, so forests are protected.
keyPoints: Saving paper means fewer trees cut
questions.explanation: Reducing demand reduces cutting of forests.

questions.q: The part of a plant cell that lies outside the cell membrane is the:
questions.explanation: The rigid cell wall surrounds the cell membrane in plant cells.

questions.q: The genetic information of the cell is stored in the:
questions.explanation: The nucleus contains chromosomes carrying genes.

questions.q: Compared with an animal cell, a mature plant cell typically has:
questions.explanation: Plant cells have a large central vacuole, while animal cells have small ones.

questions.q: What are cell organelles? Name two of them.
questions.answer: Organelles are small structures within a cell, each doing a particular job. Two examples are the nucleus and the mitochondria.
questions.explanation: Organelles divide the work of the cell.

questions.q: An animal cell cannot make its own food by photosynthesis because it:
questions.explanation: Only cells with chloroplasts can trap sunlight to make food.

questions.q: Cells in the roots of a plant have no chloroplasts. The most likely reason is that:
options: Sunlight does not reach the roots, so they do not carry out photosynthesis
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts are found where light reaches, as in leaves.

questions.q: Why is the nucleus called the control centre of a cell?
questions.answer: The nucleus holds the chromosomes with genes, which carry instructions for the cell, so it controls growth, activities and reproduction of the cell. A cell without its nucleus cannot work properly for long.
keyPoints: Controls the activities of the cell
Needed for the cell to function
questions.explanation: It acts like the brain of the cell.

questions.q: The type of reproduction in which two parents are involved is called:
questions.explanation: Sexual reproduction needs a male and a female gamete.

questions.q: The cell formed by fusion of a sperm and an egg is the:
questions.explanation: The fertilised egg is called a zygote.

questions.q: The stage of development in humans in which all the body parts can be identified is the:
questions.explanation: The embryo is called a foetus once its body parts can be identified.

questions.q: Write two differences between sexual and asexual reproduction.
questions.answer: In sexual reproduction two parents are involved and gametes fuse, so the young are different from the parents. In asexual reproduction only one parent is involved and the young are almost identical to the parent, as in Hydra budding.
keyPoints: Sexual needs two parents; asexual needs one
Asexual offspring are similar to the parent
questions.explanation: Asexual reproduction does not involve gametes.

questions.q: Frogs usually lay their eggs in water in the rainy season because:
options: Tadpoles need water to live and breathe through gills
questions.explanation: Tadpoles live in water, and their gills work only in water.

questions.q: Which statement about a zygote is correct?
options: It has only the mother's genes
It is formed by fusion of a sperm and an egg and has genes from both parents
questions.explanation: The zygote gets genetic material from both gametes.

questions.q: Why does a child look like both parents?
questions.answer: The zygote is formed by fusion of a sperm from the father and an egg from the mother, so it gets genes from both. These genes decide the features of the child.
keyPoints: Zygote from father's sperm and mother's egg
questions.explanation: Features are passed on through genes.

questions.q: Hormones are secreted by:
questions.explanation: Endocrine glands release hormones into the blood.

questions.q: The stage when the body becomes capable of reproduction is called:
questions.explanation: Puberty is the stage when sexual maturity is reached.

questions.q: The adrenal glands are located:
questions.explanation: The adrenal glands sit on top of the two kidneys.

questions.q: What is goitre and how can it be prevented?
questions.answer: Goitre is a swelling in the neck caused by a lack of iodine, which the thyroid gland needs to make thyroxine. It can be prevented by using iodised salt and eating iodine-rich food.
keyPoints: Swelling of the thyroid gland in the neck
questions.explanation: Iodine is needed by the thyroid gland.

questions.q: A teenager develops pimples on the face. What is the best advice?
options: Wash the face regularly with clean water and avoid squeezing the pimples
questions.explanation: Oily skin at puberty causes pimples, and good hygiene helps.

questions.q: When a girl has her first menstrual period, it generally means that:
options: She has reached puberty and her body is maturing for reproduction
She has become an adult in all ways
questions.explanation: The first period is a sign of puberty in girls.

questions.q: Why should adolescents stay away from tobacco, alcohol and drugs?
questions.answer: These substances harm the body and the brain, especially during the growing years. They can become a habit that is hard to break and cause diseases and problems in studies and life.
questions.explanation: Healthy habits in adolescence matter a lot.

questions.q: Which example shows a force changing the shape of an object?
options: A ball rolling on the ground
questions.explanation: Squeezing makes the sponge change its shape.

questions.q: Atmospheric pressure is measured with a:
questions.explanation: A barometer is used to measure air pressure.

questions.q: The amount of friction between two surfaces depends on:
options: The shape of the object only
The roughness of the surfaces and the force pressing them together
questions.explanation: Rougher surfaces and a greater pressing force give more friction.

questions.q: A lubricant reduces friction because it:
options: Forms a thin layer between the surfaces
Increases the force pressing on them
questions.explanation: Oil and grease keep the surfaces from rubbing directly.

questions.q: What is the difference between contact forces and non-contact forces? Give one example of each.
questions.answer: A contact force acts only when objects touch each other, such as muscular force or friction. A non-contact force acts without touching, such as gravity or the force of a magnet.
questions.explanation: Gravity is a non-contact force.

questions.q: A car skids on a wet road because:
options: A film of water reduces the friction between the tyres and the road
questions.explanation: Water between the tyres and the road reduces friction.

questions.q: A glass is filled with water and covered with a card. When it is turned upside down, the card stays in place because:
options: Atmospheric pressure pushes the card upward
questions.explanation: The upward push of the air on the card is more than the weight of the water.

questions.q: Explain how the brakes of a bicycle stop it.
questions.answer: When the brake lever is pressed, the brake pads press against the rim of the wheel. The friction between the pads and the rim opposes the motion and slows the wheel until it stops.
keyPoints: Brake pads press on the wheel rim
questions.explanation: Brakes work by increasing friction.

questions.q: Sound travels through air in the form of:
questions.explanation: Vibrations pass through air as sound waves.

questions.q: Which of the following produces sound by a vibrating air column?
questions.explanation: In a flute the air inside the tube vibrates.

questions.q: An echo is:
options: A sound that is louder than normal
The sound that is heard after reflection from a surface
questions.explanation: An echo is the repetition of a sound after it bounces back from a surface.

questions.q: The speed of sound in air is about:
questions.explanation: Sound travels at roughly 340 m/s in air at ordinary temperatures.

questions.q: Write two harmful effects of noise pollution.
questions.answer: Noise pollution can damage hearing and cause headaches and lack of sleep. It can also cause stress, anger and poor concentration.
questions.explanation: Loud noise is harmful to health.

questions.q: A boy shouts in front of a cliff and hears the echo after 2 seconds. If the speed of sound is 340 m/s, how far is the cliff?
questions.explanation: Sound travels to the cliff and back in 2 s, so the distance covered is 680 m, and the cliff is half of that, 340 m.

questions.q: A struck tuning fork sounds louder when its stem is placed on a table. Why?
options: The table vibrates along with the fork and sets more air in motion
The sound travels in a vacuum
questions.explanation: The larger surface of the table moves more air, so the sound is louder.

questions.q: How is sound produced when a drum is beaten, and why does a harder beat give a louder sound?
questions.answer: Beating the drum makes the stretched membrane vibrate, and these vibrations produce sound. A harder beat makes the membrane vibrate with a larger amplitude, so the sound is louder.
questions.explanation: Loudness depends on amplitude.

questions.q: Which device is used to find out whether a liquid conducts electricity?
questions.explanation: A simple tester has a cell and a bulb or LED connected by wires.

questions.q: Which of the following liquids is a good conductor of electricity?
questions.explanation: Salt dissolved in water makes it conduct electricity.

questions.q: A layer of metal is deposited on an object during electroplating when:
options: Current passes through a solution of a salt of that metal
The object is dipped in oil
questions.explanation: Electric current passing through the solution makes the metal deposit on the object.

questions.q: Which of the following is a chemical change caused by an electric current?
options: Deposition of copper on an electrode
questions.explanation: Deposition of copper is a new substance forming, so it is a chemical change.

questions.q: What is meant by the chemical effect of an electric current? Give two examples.
questions.answer: When electric current passes through a conducting liquid, it can cause chemical changes in it. Examples are the formation of gas bubbles at the electrodes and the deposition of a metal during electroplating.
keyPoints: Current causes chemical reactions in solutions
questions.explanation: The changes produce new substances.

questions.q: Gas bubbles appear at the electrodes when current passes through a solution. This shows that:
options: New substances (gases) are being formed, so a chemical change is occurring
questions.explanation: Formation of a gas is a sign of a chemical change.

questions.q: Which solution is most likely to make the bulb of a tester glow the brightest?
questions.explanation: Salt solution conducts well, while the others are poor conductors.

questions.q: What precautions should be taken while doing experiments with electric circuits?
questions.answer: Use only cells or batteries and never the mains supply. Keep hands dry, do not touch bare wires, and do not leave the circuit on for too long, since the wires and the liquid may get heated.
questions.explanation: Safety is essential when working with electricity.

questions.q: Light travels in:
questions.explanation: In a uniform medium such as air, light travels in straight lines.

questions.q: Which of the following is a luminous object?
questions.explanation: A luminous object gives out its own light, like the Sun.

questions.q: A ray of light strikes a plane mirror along the normal. It is reflected:
questions.explanation: The angle of incidence is zero, so the angle of reflection is also zero.

questions.q: The Richter scale is used to measure:
questions.explanation: The Richter scale gives the magnitude of an earthquake.

questions.q: What is lateral inversion?
questions.answer: Lateral inversion is the change in which the left side of an object appears as the right side in its image in a plane mirror, and vice versa. It is why writing looks reversed in a mirror.
keyPoints: Left appears as right in the image
questions.explanation: Mirrors reverse left and right, not up and down.

questions.q: Why should we not take shelter under a tall tree during a thunderstorm?
options: Tall trees attract lightning and the charge can pass through them to people nearby
questions.explanation: Lightning tends to strike the tallest objects, so a tree is dangerous.

questions.q: Two plane mirrors are placed at right angles to each other with an object between them. How many images are seen?
questions.explanation: Mirrors at 90 degrees give 360 divided by 90, minus 1, which is 3 images.

questions.q: Why do we sometimes hear crackling sounds and see small sparks when we take off a synthetic sweater in the dark?
questions.answer: Rubbing of the sweater against the body and other clothes charges it with static electricity. When the charges are released they jump as tiny sparks, which we hear as crackles, like a very small version of lightning.
keyPoints: Similar to lightning on a small scale
questions.explanation: Lightning is also a discharge of static charges.
